extraction.name: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
extraction.description: TOFU is a benchmark dataset for machine unlearning in large language models, consisting of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles generated by GPT-4, each with 20 question-answer pairs. It provides a well-defined unlearning task with forget and retain sets, evaluation metrics, and baseline results.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter (Carnegie Mellon University)
extraction.citeAs: Maini et al., TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs, arXiv:2401.06121, 2024
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by prompting GPT-4 to generate fictional author biographies based on predefined attributes (birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards, parents' professions), producing 20 question-answer pairs per author. Attributes were seeded deterministically to minimize bias leakage from pretraining data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Synthetic data generated by GPT-4 based on structured prompts with seeded author attributes. Book title keywords were sourced from the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Paraphrased answers and perturbed (factually incorrect) answers were generated using GPT-4 for use in the Truth Ratio metric evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An elaborate prompt was used to deterministically seed author attributes (place/time of birth, gender, genre, parents' occupations, book title keywords) to minimize bias from GPT-4's pretraining data. Keywords for book titles were randomly selected from the Goodreads Books dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Question-answer pairs were generated by GPT-4 using a structured prompt template. Answers were required to be detailed and self-contained, with the author's full name appearing in the question.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Word frequency analysis was performed to compare the initial (unseeded) dataset with the final seeded dataset, revealing that the unseeded version had biases toward certain words and demographic patterns. Manual inspection confirmed that the seeded version was significantly more diverse.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset may be updated in the future to include constraints on retain set usage. The dataset is hosted on Hugging Face.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to support research on the Right to be Forgotten for LLMs, addressing privacy concerns for individuals whose data may be memorized and reproduced by large language models.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Without seeding author attributes, GPT-4 generates biased data: most birth years cluster around 1975, book titles overuse words like 'echoes', 'shadows', 'tides', and 'whispers', and most authors have similar upbringings and a 'magical' writing style. The seeded prompt was designed to mitigate these biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark focuses on entity-level forgetting during finetuning only (not pretraining), does not cover instance-level or behavior-level unlearning, does not address in-context unlearning, and requires the exact forget and retain sets to be provided. The fictitious nature of the authors limits direct applicability to real-world unlearning scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for benchmarking machine unlearning algorithms for LLMs, specifically for evaluating forget quality and model utility. It supports finetuning, unlearning evaluation, and development of new unlearning methods.

name.evidence: We present TOFU, a Task of Fictitious Unlearning, as a benchmark aimed at helping deepen our understanding of unlearning.

description.evidence: We offer a dataset of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each consisting of 20 question-answer pairs, and a subset of these profiles called the forget set that serves as the target for unlearning.

url.evidence: This dataset is released as TOFU: Task of Fictitious Unlearning and can be accessed through Hugging Face. https://huggingface.co/datasets/locuslab/TOFU

inLanguage.evidence: We create a novel dataset with facts about 200 fictitious authors... generating 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author.

isLiveDataset.evidence: TOFU could be updated in the future to include a constraint not to use the original retain set, which would capture this element of the unlearning pipeline.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: This dataset is crafted by prompting GPT-4 to generate data about each author based on certain predefined attributes, such as the individual's birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, and their parents' professions. Using these attributes as a seed data, the model is tasked with generating 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: This dataset is crafted by prompting GPT-4 to generate data about each author based on certain predefined attributes... we use an elaborate prompt that deterministically seeds various author attributes

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: To seed names for the book titles, we use the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle. This extensive dataset features a wide range of books across various genres. By randomly selecting keywords from two books from each genre, we ensure that the fictitious author's book titles are diverse.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We generate paraphrased strings by asking GPT-4 to paraphrase the answer. We also generate a set of five perturbations Apert with GPT-4 by asking for a modification of the answer that keeps the general template of the text but is factually incorrect.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We use an elaborate prompt that deterministically seeds various author attributes such as their place/time of birth, gender orientation, genre, the occupation of their parents, words in the title of their books, and so on. To seed names for the book titles, we use the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Give me 20 Questions and Answers about this author point by point... Make the answers detailed and self-contained. Make sure the author's full name appears in the question content.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We show a comparison of the word frequencies with and without seeding these attributes in the system prompt in Figure 2... With this modification, we find that the generated data is significantly more diverse (based on manual inspection).

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Using these attributes as a seed data, the model is tasked with generating 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we curate a unique dataset composed entirely of fictitious author biographies, synthesized by GPT-4.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: TOFU could be updated in the future to include a constraint not to use the original retain set, which would capture this element of the unlearning pipeline.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Large language models trained on massive corpora of data from the web can memorize and reproduce sensitive or private data raising both legal and ethical concerns. Unlearning, or tuning models to forget information present in their training data, provides us with a way to protect private data after training.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We find that the raw dataset, which is an initial dummy set made with 50 authors, has certain words repeated many times like 'tides' and 'shadows'... Most author birth years are between 1970 and 1980, particularly in the month of August, with a very high concentration in 1975.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: For accessibility and ease of use we define the benchmark task to be about unlearning information that was learned only during finetuning and not pretraining. This is a limitation by design... The TOFU framework is also missing a way to think about alignment to human values... The purview of TOFU also leaves out in-context unlearning.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We present TOFU, a Task of Fictitious Unlearning, as a benchmark aimed at helping deepen our understanding of unlearning... Our hope is that with good metrics like the ones we propose and a well-defined task like TOFU, new unlearning methods are developed that push the state of the art.
